metadata.title: Who Needs Special Education Professional Development? International Trends from TALIS 2013

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2013 teacher microdata from 38 countries/partners and applies TALIS teacher sample weights to produce population-representative estimates. It also incorporates replicate weights to obtain correct standard errors under the complex survey design. The analytic sample is restricted to lower-secondary teachers and schools as defined by TALIS sampling, and the authors fit two-level logistic regression models with teachers nested within schools while including country fixed effects. For missing data in regression models, the authors used chained-equations multiple imputation (five imputed datasets) and report that non-imputed results were consistent with imputed results; therefore, the main reported estimates reflect the imputation approach pooled across datasets.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an official IEA/OECD technical report or assessment framework. It describes sampling, scaling, and instrument design rather than student-level predictive modeling. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the document's primary analytic purpose; any missing-data discussion refers to fieldwork or scaling procedures, not a single ML imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the TALIS 2013 teacher analytic sample at the lower secondary level: 121,173 teachers from 38 TALIS-participating countries and partners, surveyed via a two-stage probability design (schools selected with PPS of teachers within strata; teachers randomly selected within schools). The study does not sample schools that teach exclusively students with special needs, so teachers in such contexts are not directly represented. Outcomes are restricted to teachers’ self-reports: (i) participation in special education professional development in the last 12 months (yes/no) and impact (dichotomized to large impact vs other), and (ii) current professional development need for teaching special needs students (ordinal 1–4 dichotomized to high need vs not high need). For regression models, missingness was handled via chained-equations multiple imputation pooled across five imputed datasets; the authors state non-imputed results were consistent.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report analyzes TALIS 2013 teacher survey data to understand professional development (PD) participation, perceived impact, and current need for special education among lower-secondary teachers. The analytic sample includes 121,173 teachers nested in 1,074 schools across 38 TALIS-participating countries and partners, using a two-stage probability design (schools selected with PPS of teachers; teachers randomly sampled within schools). Outcomes are teacher self-reports: participation in special education PD in the last 12 months (yes/no), impact of that PD (dichotomized to large impact vs other), and current PD need for teaching special needs students (dichotomized to high need vs not high need). The study fits two-level logistic regression models with teachers nested within schools and includes country fixed effects; it incorporates TALIS teacher and replicate weights to reflect complex survey design. Missing data in regression models are addressed via chained-equations multiple imputation pooled across five imputed datasets, with non-imputed results reported as consistent.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD TALIS 2013 descriptive/associational report using weighted two-level logistic regression rather than an ML predictive modeling study; therefore, no ML algorithm comparison or ML target-specific performance table is extracted. The schema’s main_findings is left empty because the report does not present ML-style predictive performance metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) for an ML pipeline, and the analysis is framed as regression-based associations and descriptive trends.
